name: Constellation Energy
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Constellation is the counterparty that defines what hyperscaler firm power costs — the 20-year Microsoft PPA behind the Crane Clean Energy Center (Three Mile Island Unit 1) restart is priced by analysts at ~$112/MWh, roughly twice regional renewable rates, and the restart is running ahead of schedule toward 2027 with a $1B DOE loan and a FERC interconnection-rights waiver behind it. BACKGROUND: Spun from Exelon in 2022; completed the $16.4B Calpine acquisition January 2026, creating the largest US private-sector power producer — ~55 GW spanning the largest US nuclear fleet (~22 GW, 94.7% uptime in 2025) plus Calpine's gas and geothermal (after ~5.3 GW of DOJ-mandated divestitures to LS Power). The PPA book now includes Meta (1,121 MW Clinton, from 2027), Walmart's first nuclear PPA (176 MW Dresden), 920 MW of additional long-term deals signed in Q2 2026 alone, and CyrusOne gas-adjacent arrangements at two Calpine sites in Texas. FY2026 guidance raised to $11.50-12.50 adjusted EPS. The tension: the same record PJM capacity prices lifting earnings are driving a multi-state political backlash over consumer bills.
ecosystemRole: We assess Constellation as the price-setter for firm carbon-free power in the AI buildout — its deals establish the benchmarks every data-center energy negotiation references — and as the vendor of the scarcest product in this file: 24x7 clean baseload with a balance sheet behind it. Basis: the analyst-estimated pricing ladder its deals created (~$112/MWh for restart nuclear, ~$70/MWh for existing-reactor output, a management-stated $20-50/MWh premium band), the FERC co-location docket it forced open (the December 2025 order directing PJM to write co-location rules came from Constellation's own complaint), and ~30% of its clean baseload now under long-term contract. For BESS vendors the relevance is indirect but real: every nuclear PPA a hyperscaler signs reduces near-term appetite for firming storage at that load — and the Calpine gas fleet now gives Constellation a dispatchable product that competes directly with battery-backed alternatives.

productsAndServices.name: Nuclear fleet & long-term PPAs
productsAndServices.description: The largest US nuclear fleet: ~22 GW across 15 sites, 94.7% uptime in 2025, ~10% of US clean energy. The PPA book: Microsoft 20-year/835 MW (Crane restart, PJM grid-delivered), Meta 20-year/1,121 MW (Clinton, replacing the expiring state ZEC program from June 2027, with a 30 MW uprate), Walmart ~176 MW (Dresden, two 15-year periods from 2029/2030 — the first retailer nuclear PPA), plus 920 MW of new 15-20-year PPAs signed in Q2 2026. Fleet plan: up to 1,000 MW of uprates and relicensing into the 2070s; Dresden through ~2049-2051, Clinton through 2047, Ginna/Nine Mile Point applications filed.
productsAndServices.positioning: The reference seller of firm clean energy — the Meta deal is read by Utility Dive as 'the first of many' for existing reactors; hourly carbon-free matching (on an Azure-based platform, Microsoft the anchor customer) differentiates against annual-REC renewable sellers.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term bilateral PPAs (physical and virtual), retail supply (2.5M customer accounts, 80% of Fortune 100), hourly CFE products.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Crane online 2027 (accelerated from 2028); management expects deal flow to 'kick off with a bit of a bang' once PJM's FERC-ordered co-location rules land.

productsAndServices.name: Crane Clean Energy Center (TMI Unit 1 restart)
productsAndServices.description: The marquee project: 835 MW PWR restart (~$1.6B), renamed for late CEO Chris Crane. Status: ahead of schedule for 2027 — ~80% staffed, major inspections complete, NRC fuel license amendment approved, FERC waiver transferred 760 MW of capacity interconnection rights from retiring Eddystone units (skipping a multi-year queue), $1B DOE Energy Dominance Financing loan (November 2025). License renewal sought to at least 2054.
productsAndServices.positioning: The template for nuclear restarts nationwide — and the proof that federal financing plus regulatory accommodation can compress time-to-power for firm generation the way behind-the-fence gas does for flexible generation.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Dedicated 20-year PPA to Microsoft for PJM data centers.
productsAndServices.roadmap: NRC environmental review at draft-FONSI stage; watchdog opposition (Three Mile Island Alert) continues; operations expected 2H 2027.

productsAndServices.name: Calpine gas & geothermal fleet (data-center site power)
productsAndServices.description: Calpine brought 79 facilities and ~26 GW of gas plus the largest US geothermal fleet (the Geysers). Data-center productization is already visible: CyrusOne agreements for 380 MW (plus an exclusive 380 MW phase 2) adjacent to the Freestone Energy Center and ~400 MW at Thad Hill — power, grid connectivity, and site infrastructure sold together. New-build: Pin Oak Creek 460 MW gas COD April 2026; Pastoria solar + 80 MW/320 MWh battery.
productsAndServices.positioning: Gives Constellation the dispatchable, site-adjacent product nuclear can't offer — and re-gasifies the clean-energy story: roughly half the combined fleet is now fossil.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Site-adjacent supply agreements, ERCOT/West merchant sales, retail.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Final DOJ divestiture (Brazos Valley, $860M to LS Power) closing; >$2B annual free cash flow added per deal model.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Constellation has established the market-price ladder for firm clean power, and that this pricing power is its core asset. Basis: analyst-estimated ~$112/MWh (Microsoft/Crane restart), ~$70/MWh (Meta/Clinton existing output), a management-stated $20-50/MWh premium band for new deals, and 920 MW of PPAs signed in a single quarter — none of the prices company-disclosed, all market-defining.

(High confidence) We assess the regulatory environment, not demand, gates the next phase. Basis: FERC's Talen/Amazon rejection forced the industry pivot to front-of-meter and virtual PPAs; Constellation's own complaint produced the December 2025 order directing PJM to write co-location rules; management explicitly ties the next deal wave to that rulemaking.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the political-backlash risk to capacity revenue is material and rising. Basis: three consecutive PJM capacity auctions clearing at the administrative cap, the first RTO-wide reliability shortfall in PJM history, a 13-governor affordability coalition, and utility-bill anger contributing to 2025 election outcomes — legislated clawback of capacity upside is a live scenario for exactly the revenue stream behind the raised guidance.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the §45U nuclear PTC floor is both the foundation and a cliff. Basis: the ~$43.75/MWh floor underwrites the 'protected downside, unlimited upside' pitch through 2032 — but FY2025 already recorded 'unfavorable PTC portfolio results,' and the credit's expiry is inside the term of every PPA the company is signing.

(Low confidence) We assess Crane will hit its 2027 restart target. Basis: ahead-of-schedule staffing and inspections, the fuel-license amendment, DOE financing, and the FERC interconnection waiver all point positive — but the NRC's environmental review only reached draft-FONSI stage in mid-2026 and the restart process is regulatorily novel, with organized opposition on the docket.
